A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main sections, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–I are readable and can be matched despite formatting changes.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix I report original synthetic graph-classification experiments, label-corruption experiments, and evaluations on six TUDataset datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix I retain these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results.

M1.justification: The graph transformations, generalized Tree Mover’s Distance construction, GNN architectures, and learning procedures remain unchanged. The mathematical edits concern proofs rather than method components.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ER, BA, and SBM synthetic graphs; the same six TUDataset datasets; label corruption; and the Appendix I.4 classification task constructed using F5-TMD and MDS. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Table 1, Tables 4–6, and Figure 11, including the corresponding MPNN, cycle-feature, Sub-G, L-G, and LF-G variants. The added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix I retains the same graph-generation parameters, model configurations, training budgets, cross-validation procedures, and final-versus-best-validation evaluations. The expanded Figure 10 caption does not establish a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the label-noise and memorization analyses, depth and early-stopping comparisons, structural-distance analyses, and MDS visualizations. Relocated or reformatted figures do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 10’s placeholder caption is replaced with an explicit statement that shading represents ±1 standard deviation across 10 random splits. This clarifies uncertainty reporting for existing results; it does not establish additional runs. Other seed and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The matched tables and plots retain their reported results. For example, Table 1 still gives ER test accuracy of 0.9793 ± 0.0068 for F4-MPNN and 0.8490 ± 0.0045 for MPNN. Changes to plot transparency do not change the underlying findings.

T1.justification: Appendix E contains localized mathematical revisions: Lemma E.2 corrects a graph index, Lemma E.3 replaces m with ξ in its variance condition, and Equation (29) restores a missing exponential factor. Lemma E.1 also changes loss expressions. The main theorem statements and theoretical scope remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about task-aligned graph similarity, generalization bounds, and the potential harm of excessive expressivity. No main contribution is added or substantively strengthened.

C2.justification: Interpretations of task alignment, memorization, and structural distance remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning loose bounds, difficult cross-model comparisons, and unknown or expensive task-relevant pseudometrics.

D1.justification: Appendix I retains the same hardware, implementation, hyperparameter, and data-generation information. Both versions link to the same code repository. The new reproducibility statement reiterates existing proof and code availability without adding concrete access or implementation details.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Abbahaddou et al. (2025), and Appendix A.1 adds Kemper et al. (2025), explicitly connecting its conclusions to task-dependent expressivity. Other prominent citation changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, updates affiliations and publication information, and makes localized grammar and notation edits. One future-work sentence is removed. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting, adjusts float placement and Figure 9’s proportions, and renders uncertainty bands transparently in Figures 2, 3, 8, and 10. Figure 10 receives an informative caption instead of 'Caption'. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Replacing Figure 10’s placeholder caption and making uncertainty bands translucent improve interpretation of existing evidence. Local mathematical corrections and added related-work context also help readers check the paper. The gains are limited: the scientific framework and results are unchanged, and the loss-notation edits in Lemma E.1 leave internal inconsistencies rather than completing a comprehensive proof repair.
